usedTryThisNowFrames: Pick one live promise and write the next owner, the untested assumption, and the first follow-through check on the same line.
Compare one polished status update with one raw operating artifact and circle the fact that disappears between them.
Name one behavior you will inspect today: direct knowledge, realism, priority, follow-through, reward, coaching, or self-control.
Find one behavior you tolerate or reward today and write the rule it is teaching, whether or not you intended it.
Pick one role you influence and write the job demands first, then the person you feel most comfortable naming for it.
Put one critical role beside one live business goal and write the backup depth, retention risk, and development gap in one row.
Take one strategy sentence and add the missing how: customer, competition, capability, milestone, or sustainable economics.
Before your next review, write one question that could change the plan, not merely explain it.
Write one operating assumption beside the trigger that would make you revise the plan before the next review.
Write one decision as three linked questions: what is real, who carries it, and what follow-through proves it tomorrow.
execution-ch01: Pick one active promise. Write the next owner, the first proof point, and the assumption most likely to break before the next check-in.
execution-ch02: Ask for one raw signal behind a reassuring update. Get the name, source, and date, then decide whether the plan still deserves its color.
execution-ch03: Walk to one place where work is done. Ask what the report is missing, then choose one priority you will inspect again this week.
execution-ch04: Name one behavior your team praises and one behavior it tolerates. Change one visible consequence before the next status meeting.
execution-ch05: Choose one role that feels avoided. Write the current demand of the role, the person's real behavior, and the next honest action.
execution-ch06: Pick one critical role. Write the current business need, the ready backup, the retention risk, and the next development action.
execution-ch07: Take one strategic claim and write the customer, competitor, profit path, milestone, and capability that must make it true.
execution-ch08: Before your next review, write three questions: what do we know firsthand, what can we execute, and what changes after this meeting.
execution-ch09: Choose one goal. Write the resource, assumption, trade-off, contingency, and review date that will keep it from drifting.
execution-ch10: Open one uncomfortable status note today. Ask what is true, which process it touches, and what you will check again before Friday.
